description: "A kernel density estimate as a filled area, with an adjustable bandwidth."
categories: [Statistical]
---



`mark_density()` estimates a kernel density and fills the area beneath it. The
`adjust` argument scales the bandwidth.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p <- vplot(faithful) |>
  mark_density(x = eruptions, fill = "#3182bd", alpha = 0.6, adjust = 0.8) |>
  labs(title = "Old Faithful eruption density", x = "eruption (min)")
```
:::

## Histograms and frequency polygons

`mark_histogram()` bins the way ggplot2 does. `binwidth` sets the width of each
bin and `boundary` pins where the bins start, so the bars line up with round
numbers instead of with the minimum of the data.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
p_hist <- vplot(faithful) |>
  mark_histogram(x = eruptions, binwidth = 0.25, boundary = 1.5,
                 fill = "#3182bd") |>
  labs(title = "Old Faithful eruptions in quarter-minute bins",
       x = "eruption (min)")
```
:::



::: {.cell}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![](figs/density-histogram.png){width=100%}
:::
:::


`mark_freqpoly()` takes the same binning arguments and joins the bin counts
into a line, one per group, with an empty bin at each end so every line starts
and ends on zero. Overlaid lines compare groups far better than stacked bars.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
peng <- na.omit(datasets::penguins)

p_poly <- vplot(peng) |>
  mark_freqpoly(x = flipper_len, color = species, binwidth = 4,
                boundary = 170, linewidth = 1) |>
  labs(title = "Flipper length by species", x = "flipper (mm)",
       y = "penguins")
```
:::
